categories.name: SLURM step cancelled / drain / preemption
categories.description: Clean external cancellation by the scheduler - scancel, requeue, drain, preemption or a wall-clock timeout - with no application fault. Either surface is sufficient on its own. (a) A slurmstepd marker, e.g. "*** STEP <id> ON <node> CANCELLED AT <time> ***", with or without a stated reason, sometimes as the only content in an otherwise empty log. (b) Healthy iterations to the very end, then SIGTERM across many ranks, after which interpreter teardown emits tracebacks that read like application errors: "Exception ignored in atexit callback", weakref finalizer failures, TypeError/AttributeError on None as module globals are destroyed - artifacts of the kill, not its cause. If the stated reason is node failure, use cat 2 instead.

categories.name: Node failure / SLURM externally terminated
categories.description: SLURM 'CANCELLED DUE TO NODE FAILURE' or other external node termination.

categories.name: Off-file termination / external teardown (cause not in log)
categories.description: A real termination whose cause is not in this log. Training progresses normally, then only downstream surfaces appear and no initiating fault: an external-signal faulthandler dump, TCPStore connection resets as surviving ranks notice a peer vanish, "destroy_process_group() was not called before program exit" warnings at an abrupt exit, or atexit teardown noise. Completed iterations are the key signal - they prove rendezvous and setup already succeeded, so a later store or teardown error is a symptom rather than the cause. Usually a rank was killed, preempted or lost with its node, and the applog never sees why. If the log carries an explicit scheduler marker or SIGTERM across many ranks, use cat 1; if no iteration ever completed, use cat 12.

categories.name: No failure observed / clean planned exit
categories.description: Whole-file scan finds no failure: the run reached its exit_interval / final iteration, saved the final checkpoint, logged training energy, and only benign teardown (destroy_process_group / CudaIPC cleanup) follows. Includes the reset_opt_norm 'Unexpected keys' benign-WARNING trap and recovered-then-clean runs.

categories.name: Incomplete / truncated log
categories.description: Whole-file scan finds no failure signal and the log has no clean ending; likely a log-collection failure.

categories.name: NVRx used (multi-cycle, deferred)
categories.description: ft_launcher restarted the worker group in-job; one file concatenates multiple training cycles with separate root causes.

categories.name: NVLink / GPU error
categories.description: Uncorrectable NVLink/GPU hardware error (Xid, ECC DBE, peer-access failure); the device fault may be transient and clear on an in-place restart.

categories.name: IB port flap / NCCL watchdog timeout
categories.description: IB port error / RDMA retry exhaustion killing collectives; the port flap is typically transient and clears on an in-place restart.

categories.name: Container / Pyxis setup failure
categories.description: Container never started (pyxis couldn't start container / enroot failure); transient node-local runtime vs bad image undecidable from one log.

categories.name: Early/startup NCCL init or checkpoint-load timeout
categories.description: NCCL init / checkpoint-load collective timeout before the first completed training iteration; true cause usually not in this log.

categories.name: NCCL timeout mid-training
categories.description: Watchdog collective timeout after at least one completed iteration; consequence-class symptom, upstream cause often absent from the log.

categories.name: Distributed rendezvous / TCPStore socket timeout
categories.description: c10d/TCPStore rendezvous or socket failure during process-group setup, before training progresses: the store never comes up, or it fails while ranks are still joining. When store errors are the only failure surface, pick this with reduced confidence rather than declining to classify, even if the initiating rank's own output is absent. Two exclusions. If an upstream fault appears earlier in the log, pick that category. And if training iterations completed before the store errors began, rendezvous had already succeeded, so the store failed because something else died first - that is cat 3, not this.

categories.name: NCCL remote process exited / network error / bootstrap Message-truncated
categories.description: NCCL Error 6 (remote peer exited); infrastructure/peer failure. Also covers NCCL bootstrap/transport corruption ('Message truncated : received N bytes instead of M') during any distributed-checkpoint gather_object communicator setup - both LOAD-side startup and async-finalize save-side - where a downstream rank0 Segmentation fault in the same stack is NOT the root.

categories.name: OSError Errno 98 / port bind race
categories.description: Fatal port-bind failure (EADDRINUSE) at the rendezvous master; startup race, job died at bind with no progress.

categories.name: DataLoader worker I/O failure (Bus error, BrokenPipe, Lustre or NIC)
categories.description: Transient data-path I/O failure inside a DataLoader worker: Bus error, BrokenPipeError (Errno 108 transport endpoint shutdown) on Lustre-backed .bin readinto, /dev/shm exhaustion, or fatal Lustre read. Distinguishes from cat 16 by occurring in the DataLoader worker path.

categories.name: Filesystem I/O error / Lustre or node-local FS / import visibility
categories.description: Transient filesystem error on a NON-checkpoint path: Lustre I/O stall (OSError Errno 5), missing dataset cache from filesystem-visibility lag, or ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError where the failing import path lives on a network-mounted code tree. Missing CHECKPOINT paths are cat 22.

categories.name: Dataset missing indexed data files
categories.description: Dataset .idx/.bin files missing at dataset init; deterministic against the same config until dataset path/files are fixed.

categories.name: PermissionError / dataset cache or filesystem permission
categories.description: Deterministic permission-denied (EACCES/Errno 13) on dataset cache or filesystem path.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / transient async-write I/O
categories.description: Transient I/O failure during the checkpoint async-save path on a checkpoint directory: filesystem_async 'Local process 0 encountered an error', PyTorch inline_container position mismatch, BrokenPipeError Errno 108 from a writer, OSError Errno 5 (Input/output error). Prefer this over cat 16 whenever the failing path is a checkpoint directory and the mechanism is on the write side, even if the surface is generic filesystem I/O. Load-side checkpoint I/O errors that do not fit cat 10 (early/startup timeout) route to cat 16 (Filesystem I/O) instead. This category does not cover failures whose mechanism is memory exhaustion: if the checkpoint path fails because a CUDA or NCCL allocation could not be satisfied, that is a CUDA OOM category even though the failing path is the checkpoint path.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / corrupt checkpoint metadata on load
categories.description: Garbled checkpoint metadata buffer at load (UnpicklingError/UnicodeDecodeError); transient corruption, checkpoint likely reusable on healthy nodes.

categories.name: Post-checkpoint progress-log assertion
categories.description: Assertion raised by progress-log bookkeeping after a checkpoint resume: the iteration or sample counts recorded in the progress log disagree with the state of the checkpoint being resumed. Bookkeeping is what failed, not the configuration or the model code, and the last committed checkpoint is intact, so restart from it is appropriate. Not for assertions that check a configuration value - global batch size divisibility, world size, parallelism dimensions - which fail identically on an unchanged retry and belong in cat 28, even when they first fire after a resume.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / missing checkpoint path
categories.description: Missing checkpoint path; cannot self-heal by restarting.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / deterministic checkpoint format or shape mismatch
categories.description: Checkpoint-load shape/key/TP-PP mismatch with zero completed iterations; deterministic against same checkpoint + code/config.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / async-save finalize code error
categories.description: Deterministic code error (e.g. NoneType AttributeError) in the post-training async-save FINALIZE path.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / save-path native crash (PyTorchStreamWriter)
categories.description: Native SIGSEGV in PyTorchStreamWriter::writeRecord during the first torch_dist checkpoint save; structural serializer buffer overrun deterministic against unchanged shape/config.

categories.name: CUDA OOM during checkpoint async-save
categories.description: CUDA OOM inside the async checkpoint-save path on a near-full GPU. An unchanged workload will keep hitting the same allocation ceiling on retry.

categories.name: Bad token / gradient Inf or NaN
categories.description: Non-finite gradient/loss from a bad token or transient overflow.

categories.name: Launch config or workload code deterministic error
categories.description: Deterministic runtime error inside already-loaded workload code that will recur on unchanged retry: TypeError/AttributeError on None value threaded through model code (e.g. float(None) in moe_layer postprocess), missing MASTER_ADDR, argparse error, or world-size mismatch. Excludes ModuleNotFoundError / ImportError where the failing import path resolves under Lustre or a mounted network filesystem - those are cat 16 (filesystem visibility), not a workload code fault, even if no adjacent FileNotFoundError is present on the same line. Also excludes tracebacks demonstrably raised during interpreter shutdown - inside "Exception ignored", atexit or weakref teardown frames - which are the wake of an external kill (cat 1) rather than a code fault. Earlier successful iterations do not by themselves disqualify this category: a deterministic fault can first surface late, when an evaluation step runs, a data-dependent branch is taken, or a scheduled value such as data_parallel_size changes and a divisibility assertion then fails. Such a fault recurs under the resulting configuration, so it belongs here.

categories.name: Triton cubin / TorchInductor software toolchain error
categories.description: Triton autotuner KeyError 'Unknown key: cubin' on mamba_ssm kernels, or TorchInductor StaticCudaLauncher 'CUDA driver error: file not found' at JIT warmup. Clean Python exceptions, multi-node, deterministic in-container: the same compilation fails on every rank that attempts it, so an unchanged retry reproduces it. Requires one of those two signatures. A compile or cache failure that hits only a few ranks while the rest compile the same kernel is cat 39, not this - a toolchain that is genuinely broken in-container fails every rank that attempts the compilation, not a small subset of them.

categories.name: CUDA illegal op in CUDA graph capture
categories.description: Illegal CUDA operation during graph capture; deterministic code bug on the same code path.

categories.name: CPU OOM / Linux OOM killer
categories.description: Host memory exhausted: bare 'Killed' on one or more ranks corroborated by a slurmstepd 'Detected N oom_kill events ... Some of the step tasks have been OOM Killed' record (the oom_kill line often appears far below the 'Killed' lines). Host memory exhaustion is deterministic for the same job/config: an unchanged retry is expected to hit the same ceiling unless resources or configuration change.

categories.name: CUDA OOM
categories.description: Device OOM at fixed batch/config. A CUDA OOM under an unchanged workload is highly likely to reproduce on the next attempt, and the outcome is stable across attempts.

categories.name: CUDA unspecified launch failure
categories.description: cudaErrorLaunchFailure; a single log cannot separate transient hardware/runtime state from a deterministic kernel/code bug.

categories.name: Segmentation fault / native runtime crash
categories.description: SIGSEGV in native code with no accompanying hardware signal and no self-reported corruption guard, usually confined to a single rank. A wild or high faulting address, rather than a near-null offset, points at memory corruption rather than a null dereference; host-side pinned-allocator and dataset-index paths are common sites. A single log cannot separate a library race from host-memory corruption.

categories.name: Node-local native SIGBUS (Triton/TE native kernel)
categories.description: Native SIGBUS confined to one node or tray, in two forms: during Triton JIT .so dlopen/mmap at kernel load, before any iteration completes; or mid-training inside a TE/Triton native kernel, where only that node's ranks die while thousands of peers keep running. The node-local blast radius is the discriminator, and points at a node-local hardware or memory fault rather than a workload bug.

categories.name: Startup native SIGSEGV / torch pin_memory host-allocator
categories.description: Native SIGSEGV 'address not mapped to object at address 0x8' (null-ptr deref) with a byte-identical backtrace through at::native::_pin_memory into the libtorch_cuda CachingHostAllocator pinned-map operator[], fired at [before the start of training step] with zero completed iterations. pin_cpu_grads/pin_cpu_params=True forces the path in-log; crashing node sets differ across jobs (rules out node-local hardware); reproduces every rerun. 20 samples = 11 unique files (9 md5 mirror pairs).

categories.name: Native heap corruption / glibc malloc abort
categories.description: Native glibc heap-integrity abort ("malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected") on a rank pre-first-iter; deterministic in-process heap corruption traceable to the initialization software stack, recurs on unchanged code/library/container image.

categories.name: Suspected SDC / DP-replica weight-hash mismatch
categories.description: DP-replica weight-hash mismatch (suspected silent data corruption); restart from last good checkpoint is plausibly safe.

categories.name: Transient JIT compile-cache artifact failure
categories.description: A compiled-kernel artifact is unreadable or unusable on a small minority of ranks while the rest of the job compiles the same kernel successfully. Seen as a JSONDecodeError 'Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' raised from Triton's CompiledKernel.__init__ or _precompile_config, which means the cached metadata file was empty; as an InductorError 'CUDA driver error: device kernel image is invalid'. Each leaves an artifact behind that cannot be read or loaded. The rank fraction is the discriminator and it is required: compare the failing rank count against the job's observed rank count, and pick this only when the failures are a small minority. A small subset failing while the overwhelming majority compile the same kernel is a write race on a shared cache directory; every attempting rank failing is a broken toolchain and belongs in cat 29. Judge the ratio, not an absolute count: job sizes differ, so what matters is that the failures are a minority of the ranks that attempted the same compilation. Partially written cache artifacts are rewritten or recompiled on the next attempt, so the retry is expected to differ. Zero completed iterations does not argue against this: compilation happens at warmup and again whenever a new shape is traced, so it can also strike a job that has been training for some time. A JIT compiler invocation that fails to complete, rather than an artifact that cannot be read, is cat 40.

categories.name: JIT toolchain invocation failure on isolated ranks
categories.description: A just-in-time compiler invocation does not complete, on a small minority of ranks, and the compiler's own diagnostics are absent from the log. Seen as a RuntimeError 'Failed to compile the code' from a deep_ep hybrid_ep JIT build, or an equivalent wrapper that reports the command it ran but not what the compiler said. The rank fraction is required and rules out the deterministic reading: bad source, bad flags or an unsupported architecture fail every rank that attempts the same build, so one rank of thousands means the inputs compile. Compare the failing rank count against the job's observed rank count. A single log cannot separate a node-local resource condition - output directory full, memory pressure, a concurrent write to the same target - from a genuine toolchain fault, because the diagnostic that would distinguish them was never recorded. Whether the next attempt hits the same condition is not determinable from this log. Distinct from cat 39, where a compiled artifact exists but is empty or unusable; here the artifact was never produced. Distinct from cat 29, which requires a compilation that fails on every rank attempting it.

categories.name: DataLoader worker lost / multiprocessing IPC peer failure
categories.description: A data-pipeline feeder thread fails because the worker process it was reading from is gone, after training has already progressed. The stack runs through a queue feed into multiprocessing IPC: _feed_queue or a QueueThread, queue.get, _ForkingPickler.loads, rebuild_storage_fd, resource_sharer.detach, get_connection, Client, answer_challenge, recv_bytes. It ends on EOFError, often with no message at all, or ConnectionResetError [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer, or BrokenPipeError, on a minority of ranks while the rest keep running. What killed the worker is not in this log: only the surviving thread's view of the peer disappearing is recorded. Not cat 28: no launch configuration and no workload code raised here. The frames are Python's own multiprocessing and torch's reduction machinery, reached through an unmodified data pipeline that had been feeding batches successfully. Not cat 15, which needs an I/O failure visible inside the worker - a Bus error, /dev/shm exhaustion, or a failed read of a backing file. Here the worker is simply absent and no I/O error of its own appears. Prefer this over cat 3, which says only that the cause is off-file: both are true, and this one also names the mechanism that failed.

categories.name: Fabric resource allocation failure at init (NVLS / multicast)
categories.description: A node cannot acquire a fabric resource while communicators are being built, before any iteration completes: NCCL WARN from nvlsAllocateMem 'Failed to bind NVLink SHARP (NVLS) Multicast memory', commonly with CUDA error 802 'system not yet initialized', or an equivalent multicast/fabric allocation failure on one node. Its own ranks then raise a DistBackendError 'unhandled cuda error' and every other rank reports 'remote process exited or there was a network error'. Those peer reports are the cascade, not the cause - pick this rather than cat 13 when an allocation failure names the node that went first. Zero completed iterations is required: the allocation is attempted during setup, so a job that reached training did not fail this way. Use cat 7 instead when the log carries an Xid, ECC or peer-access hardware fault rather than an allocation refusal. The refusal is bound to one node or rack; the workload is unmodified and runs elsewhere, which is what separates this from a workload fault.
